**LUMINA CLINICAL RESEARCH PTE. LTD.**
**SITE OPERATIONS MANUAL – SINGAPORE CLINICAL TRIAL SITE (SCTS / SITE 01)**

**Document ID:** SOM-SG-001
**Version:** 4.2
**Effective Date:** 02 June 2025
**Owner:** Director, Site Operations
**Approver:** Head of Clinical Operations, APAC

---

**VERSION HISTORY TABLE**

| Version | Effective Date | Description of Change | Author |
|---------|----------------|-----------------------|--------|
| 1.0 | 15 Mar 2021 | Initial release. | J. Tan |
| 2.0 | 10 Sep 2022 | Updated Section 5 (Informed Consent) to align with HSA guidance; added Section 8 (Site Activation). | M. Lim |
| 3.0 | 05 Jan 2024 | Revised data entry timelines; clarified delegation of authority log requirements. | P. Ramesh |
| 4.0 | 18 Nov 2024 | Major re-format; added telemetry/equipment checks to Section 7. | A. Koh |

| 4.2 | 02 Jun 2025 | Updated site status to active; incorporated feedback from internal audit Q1. | A. Koh |

---

**1. INTRODUCTION & PURPOSE**

1.1 This manual defines the procedures and standards for the conduct of clinical trials at the Singapore Clinical Trial Site (SCTS), also referred to as Site 01. It applies to all staff, contractors, and visiting monitors engaged in trial-related activities at the site.

1.2 The purpose of this manual is to ensure that all activities are performed in accordance with the International Council for Harmonisation Good Clinical Practice (ICH GCP) guidelines, the Singapore Health Sciences Authority (HSA) regulations, and Lumina Clinical Research corporate policies.

1.3 The Site Operations Manual records that Singapore Clinical Trial Site site_status is active. Record status: current. This is the current controlled entry and supersedes any previous status notations. All staff must verify the current version of this manual before commencing trial activities.

1.4 Questions regarding the interpretation of this manual should be directed to the Site Operations Director. Proposed changes must be submitted in writing using the Document Change Request form (SOM-F001).

---

**2. SITE ORGANIZATION & RESPONSIBILITIES**

2.1 The site operates under the leadership of the Principal Investigator (PI), who has overall responsibility for the conduct of the trial at the site.

2.2 Key roles and responsibilities:

| Role | Responsibility |
|------|----------------|
| Principal Investigator | Medical oversight, final responsibility for participant safety and data integrity. |
| Sub-Investigators | Delegated medical duties as per the Delegation of Authority Log. |
| Site Coordinator | Day-to-day trial management, scheduling, regulatory document maintenance. |
| Research Nurse | Participant care, sample collection, visit procedures. |
| Data Entry Clerk | Accurate and timely entry of data into the Electronic Case Report Form (eCRF). |
| Pharmacy Staff | Investigational Product (IP) handling, storage, and accountability. |
| Regulatory Affairs Officer | Submission of documents to HSA and ethics committee (EC). |

2.3 The Delegation of Authority Log must be maintained and signed by the PI. Any change in staff responsibilities must be documented and dated.

---

**3. ENROLLMENT PROCEDURES**

3.1 **Screening**
3.1.1 Potential participants are identified through approved recruitment materials or physician referral. All recruitment materials must be approved by the EC prior to use.
3.1.2 The Site Coordinator schedules a screening visit. The participant must be given the Informed Consent Form (ICF) and a copy of the Participant Information Sheet at least 24 hours prior to the screening visit, unless the protocol specifies a shorter period.
3.1.3 Screening procedures, including medical history, physical examination, and laboratory tests, must be performed only after written informed consent is obtained.
4.1 Monitoring visits are conducted by the Clinical Research Associate (CRA) or their delegate to verify that the trial is conducted in accordance with the protocol, Good Clinical Practice (GCP), applicable regulatory requirements, and this manual. The CRA serves as the primary point of contact between the site and the sponsor.

4.2 Types of monitoring visits:

| Visit Type | Purpose | Typical Frequency |
|------------|---------|-------------------|
| Site Initiation Visit (SIV) | Training on protocol, procedures, and IP handling prior to first participant enrollment. | Once, before enrollment begins |
| Routine Monitoring Visit | Ongoing review of participant records, IP accountability, and regulatory documents. | As per Monitoring Plan (e.g., every 4–6 weeks) |
| Close-out Visit | Final verification, return of IP, and confirmation that all outstanding items are resolved. | At trial completion |

4.3 The CRA shall notify the Site Coordinator at least 3 working days before a scheduled monitoring visit, unless the visit is triggered by an urgent safety or compliance concern. Urgent visits may occur without prior notice.

4.4 During a monitoring visit, the CRA will review, at minimum:

4.4.1 Source documents for enrolled participants, including signed informed consent forms, medical records, and laboratory reports.

4.4.2 eCRF entries against source data for accuracy and completeness.

4.4.3 IP accountability records, including dispensing logs, temperature logs, and returns.

4.4.4 Regulatory documents, including the Delegation of Authority Log, staff qualifications, and training records.

4.4.5 Adverse event (AE) and serious adverse event (SAE) documentation and reporting timelines.

4.5 Site staff shall make available all requested documents and provide a quiet workspace for the CRA. The Site Coordinator is responsible for coordinating access to source documents and ensuring that staff are available to answer questions.

4.6 The CRA will document findings in a Monitoring Visit Report. The report will note the date of the visit, the scope of review, findings, and any required corrective and preventive actions (CAPAs).

4.7 Monitoring Visit Report notes Clinical Research Associate monitoring_visit_status is completed. Record status: historical. The report is appended to this manual as Attachment A (latest version) and is considered part of the site's trial master file.

4.8 Follow-up actions identified during a monitoring visit must be completed within the timeframe specified in the report. The Site Coordinator shall track action items and confirm resolution in writing to the CRA. Unresolved findings may be escalated to the PI and, if necessary, to the sponsor.

4.9 The PI is responsible for ensuring that monitoring visits can be conducted as scheduled and that findings are addressed in a timely manner.

---

**5. DOCUMENTATION REQUIREMENTS FOR MONITORING VISIT REPORTS**

5.1 Each Monitoring Visit Report shall be signed and dated by the CRA. The report shall include:

5.1.1 Visit identification: visit number, date(s) of visit, and type of visit.

5.1.2 Participants reviewed: list of participant numbers and the extent of verification performed.

5.1.3 Findings: categorized as (a) no findings, (b) minor observations, or (c) major observations requiring CAPA.

5.1.4 Action items: description, responsible person, and due date.

5.1.5 Summary of IP accountability, including any discrepancies.

5.2 The report shall be distributed to the PI and Site Coordinator within 10 working days of the visit. A copy shall be filed in the regulatory binder.

5.3 The site shall retain all Monitoring Visit Reports for at least the duration required by applicable regulations and the sponsor's retention policy.
**6. VISIT SCHEDULING, CANCELLATION AND RESCHEDULING**

6.1 The Site Coordinator shall maintain a master visit schedule for the duration of the study. The schedule shall list, for each planned visit: the visit type (routine monitoring, site qualification, site initiation, close-out, or other), the expected date, the assigned Clinical Research Associate (CRA), and the current status.

6.2 A copy of the master visit schedule shall be provided to the CRA at the start of each monitoring visit and updated, if necessary, at the end of the visit. The schedule shall also be available for review by the PI upon request.

6.3 Scheduling of monitoring visits shall be coordinated between the Site Coordinator and the CRA. The Site Coordinator shall confirm the proposed visit dates with the PI and the pharmacy, as applicable, before confirming the visit with the CRA.

6.4 The site shall make every reasonable effort to accommodate the proposed visit dates. If a proposed date conflicts with a scheduled participant visit, a public holiday, or a planned site closure, the Site Coordinator shall inform the CRA within two working days of receiving the proposed schedule and propose alternative dates.

6.5 Cancellation Policy

6.5.1 Site Operations Manual specifies Lumina Clinical Research cancellation_policy is 48 hours notice. Record status: current. The 48-hour notice period is measured from the time the cancellation notification is sent by the Site Coordinator to the CRA and the CRO's monitoring department.

6.5.2 A cancellation is defined as the notification by the site that a scheduled monitoring visit will not occur on the agreed date. Cancellations shall be communicated in writing by email, with a read receipt requested, and shall include the visit number and the reason for cancellation.

6.5.3 If a visit is cancelled with less than 48 hours notice, the site shall document the reason and the circumstances in the visit schedule and, upon request, provide a written explanation to the CRO. Repeated late cancellations may result in a review of the site's scheduling practices.

6.5.4 Cancellations requested by the CRA or the CRO are not subject to this policy. In such cases, the CRA shall provide a revised schedule to the Site Coordinator as soon as practicable.

6.5.5 The cancellation policy is subject to change. The current version of this policy is in effect as of the date of this manual. Any proposed change shall be communicated in writing to the site at least 30 days before the effective date of the change.

6.6 Rescheduling Guidelines

6.6.1 When a visit is cancelled, the Site Coordinator shall work with the CRA to identify a mutually agreeable alternative date. The alternative date shall be recorded in the master visit schedule as a rescheduled visit, with the original visit number retained and the suffix "R" added (e.g., Visit 4R).

6.6.2 The rescheduled visit shall take place as soon as practicable, and in any case, not later than 30 calendar days after the original scheduled date, unless a longer delay is approved in writing by the CRO.

6.6.3 If the rescheduled date falls on a date when the site is closed, the Site Coordinator shall notify the CRA at the time of rescheduling.

6.6.4 The reason for the rescheduling shall be recorded in the visit schedule using the following codes:

6.6.4.1 "PI" – PI unavailable.

6.6.4.2 "SITE" – Site closure or staff unavailability.

6.6.4.3 "PT" – Participant visit conflict requiring site staff attention.

6.6.4.4 "CRA" – CRA unavailability (initiated by CRO).

6.6.4.5 "OTHER" – Any other reason, with a brief description.

6.6.5 A rescheduled visit shall not count as a separate visit for the purpose of the monitoring plan. The original visit number and the "R" suffix shall be used consistently in all correspondence and reports.
7.0 Data Entry and Source Document Handling

7.1 General Principles

7.1.1 All data entry shall be performed in accordance with the protocol, the Clinical Data Management Plan, and applicable regulatory requirements. The source document is the primary record of participant data, and the eCRF is a transcription of that source data.

7.1.2 Source data shall be entered into the eCRF in real time, or as soon as practicable after the data is generated. In no case shall data entry be delayed more than 5 business days from the date of the source document, unless prior written approval has been obtained from the CRO.

7.1.3 The Site Coordinator is responsible for ensuring that all data entry is complete, accurate, and consistent with the source documents. The Principal Investigator retains ultimate responsibility for the accuracy and integrity of the data.

7.1.4 Only authorised site staff who have completed the required training and have been delegated data entry responsibilities on the Delegation of Authority Log shall perform data entry. The Site Coordinator shall maintain a current list of authorised data entry personnel.

7.1.5 Data entry shall be performed in a quiet, private area of the site where the eCRF screen cannot be viewed by unauthorised persons. Participant confidentiality shall be maintained at all times.

7.2 Data Entry Procedures

7.2.1 Prior to initiating data entry for a participant, the data entry staff shall verify the following:

7.2.1.1 The participant has signed and dated the current approved Informed Consent Form.

7.2.1.2 The participant has been assigned a valid Participant Identification Number.

7.2.1.3 The visit has been completed and the source documents are available.

7.2.2 Data shall be entered into the eCRF exactly as recorded in the source documents. Abbreviations, units, and decimal places shall be transcribed without modification, unless a data entry convention has been documented and approved by the CRO.

7.2.3 All fields in the eCRF shall be completed. If a field is not applicable, the appropriate code (e.g., "NA" or "ND") shall be entered in accordance with the eCRF Completion Guidelines. Fields left blank may generate queries.

7.2.4 Measurements shall be entered in the units specified in the eCRF. Where the source document records a measurement in different units, the data entry staff shall convert the value and record the conversion in the source document, including the date and initials of the person performing the conversion.

7.2.5 If a value in the source document is illegible, the data entry staff shall not guess. The source document shall be returned to the individual who generated the data for clarification. The clarification shall be made in accordance with Section 7.4 (Corrections to Source Documents).

7.2.6 Data entry shall be performed on a per-visit basis. The eCRF for a visit shall be completed and signed before the next scheduled visit, unless the monitoring plan specifies otherwise.

7.2.7 The eCRF shall be signed and dated by the authorised data entry staff upon completion of data entry for each visit. The electronic signature shall include the date and time of the signature.

7.3 eCRF Access and Security

7.3.1 Access to the eCRF system shall be controlled by unique user IDs and passwords. Passwords shall be changed at least every 90 days and shall not be shared with or disclosed to any other person.

7.3.2 The Site Coordinator shall notify the CRO immediately, and in any case within 24 hours, if any authorised user leaves the site, is reassigned, or is suspected of unauthorised access.

7.3.3 The eCRF system shall only be accessed from site computers that have current antivirus software and operating system updates. Remote access to the eCRF is not permitted unless approved in writing by the CRO.
7.4 Corrections to Source Documents

7.4.1 Corrections to source documents shall be made using a single line drawn through the erroneous entry, leaving the original entry legible. The correct value shall be written adjacent to the original entry, followed by the date of the correction and the initials of the person making the correction.

7.4.2 Correction fluid, correction tape, erasers, or any other means of obliterating the original entry shall not be used on source documents.

7.4.3 If a correction is required after the source document has been scanned or otherwise archived, the correction shall be made on a new version of the document, and the previous version shall be retained in the site files with a cross-reference to the new version. The new version shall indicate the date and reason for the correction.

7.4.4 Where a source document is an electronic record, corrections shall be made using the audit trail function of the applicable system. The audit trail shall capture the original value, the corrected value, the date and time of the correction, and the user ID of the person making the correction. No electronic source data shall be overwritten without an audit trail entry.

7.4.5 The Investigator or designee shall be responsible for ensuring that corrections to source documents are made in a timely manner and that the corrected data is reflected in the eCRF at the next available data entry session.

7.4.6 Queries issued by the CRO or data management team regarding source data shall be resolved within 5 working days of receipt. If resolution requires clarification from the participant or an external provider, the Site Coordinator shall document the reason for the delay and provide an estimated resolution date.

7.5 Source Document Retention

7.5.1 Source documents shall be retained at the site for at least 15 years after the completion of the study, or longer if required by applicable regulations or the study contract.

7.5.2 Source documents shall be stored in a locked, fire-resistant filing cabinet or in a secure electronic repository with role-based access. The Site Director shall maintain an inventory of all source documents, including their physical or electronic location.

7.5.3 No source document shall be removed from the site without prior written approval from the Site Director, except when required for audit or regulatory inspection. In such cases, a receipt shall be issued and a copy retained at the site.

7.5.4 At the close of the study, the Site Coordinator shall prepare a complete set of source documents for archiving. The archive package shall include a cover sheet listing the contents and the date of archiving.

8.0 PHARMACY AND INVESTIGATIONAL PRODUCT MANAGEMENT

8.1 General Principles

8.1.1 The handling of investigational product (IP) shall comply with the protocol, the Investigator's Brochure, and applicable regulatory requirements. The Site Pharmacist or designee shall be responsible for the receipt, storage, dispensing, and return of IP.

8.1.2 IP shall only be administered to participants who have provided informed consent and who meet the eligibility criteria specified in the protocol.

8.1.3 Any deviation from the IP handling procedures described in this manual shall be documented and reported to the Sponsor in accordance with Section 8.7 (Deviations and Non-Compliance).

8.2 Receipt of Investigational Product

8.2.1 Upon receipt of an IP shipment, the Site Pharmacist or designee shall inspect the shipment for damage, verify the contents against the packing list, and confirm that the temperature monitoring device (if included) has not been activated beyond the allowable range.

8.2.2 The receipt shall be documented on the Investigational Product Receipt Log (Appendix C). The log shall include the date and time of receipt, the shipment number, the quantity received, the lot number(s), and the condition of the shipment.

We are submitting the above-referenced substantial amendment to the Health Sciences Authority for review and approval. This submission is made in accordance with the Singapore Guideline for Clinical Trials (SGCG) and the applicable provisions of the Health Products (Clinical Trials) Regulations.

The amendment introduces the following key changes to the protocol:

1. **Primary Endpoint Analysis Window:** The time window for the primary endpoint assessment has been revised from Week 12 to Week 16. This change is supported by emerging blinded data on the trajectory of the biomarker response and is intended to capture the maximal treatment effect.

2. **Criteria for Dose Interruption:** The criteria for dose interruption have been clarified to include a single occurrence of Grade 3 neutropenia lasting more than 5 days, or any Grade 4 neutropenia. Previously, the criteria required two separate occurrences of Grade 3 neutropenia.

3. **Concomitant Medication Restrictions:** The list of prohibited concomitant medications has been updated to include strong CYP3A4 inducers. This update aligns with the latest pharmacokinetic data from the ongoing Phase 1 study.

4. **Clarification on Participant Withdrawal:** Language has been added to clarify that participants who withdraw consent for the interventional portion of the study will be asked to consent to continued follow-up for safety and survival endpoints, where permitted by local regulations.

The rationale for each change is detailed in the accompanying Amendment Summary and the tracked-changes version of the protocol. The clean version of the protocol (Version 3.2) is also enclosed.

We respectfully request HSA approval of this amendment. Should you require any further information or clarification, please do not hesitate to contact the undersigned.

**SITE OPERATIONS MANUAL – SINGAPORE CLINICAL TRIAL SITE (SCTS / SITE 01)**

**1. INTRODUCTION & PURPOSE**

1.1 This manual defines the procedures and standards for the conduct of clinical trials at the Singapore Clinical Trial Site (SCTS), also referred to as Site 01. It applies to all staff, contractors, and visiting monitors engaged in trial-related activities at the site.

1.2 The purpose of this manual is to ensure that all activities are performed in accordance with the International Council for Harmonisation Good Clinical Practice (ICH GCP) guidelines, the Singapore Health Sciences Authority (HSA) regulations, and Lumina Clinical Research corporate policies.

1.3 The Site Operations Manual records that Singapore Clinical Trial Site site_status is active. Record status: current. This is the current controlled entry and supersedes any previous status notations. All staff must verify the current version of this manual before commencing trial activities.

1.4 Questions regarding the interpretation of this manual should be directed to the Site Operations Director. Proposed changes must be submitted in writing using the Document Change Request form (SOM-F001).

---

**2. SITE ORGANIZATION & RESPONSIBILITIES**

2.1 The site operates under the leadership of the Principal Investigator (PI), who has overall responsibility for the conduct of the trial at the site.

2.2 Key roles and responsibilities:

| Role | Responsibility |
|------|----------------|
| Principal Investigator | Medical oversight, final responsibility for participant safety and data integrity. |
| Sub-Investigators | Delegated medical duties as per the Delegation of Authority Log. |
| Site Coordinator | Day-to-day trial management, scheduling, regulatory document maintenance. |
| Research Nurse | Participant care, sample collection, visit procedures. |
| Data Entry Clerk | Accurate and timely entry of data into the Electronic Case Report Form (eCRF). |
| Pharmacy Staff | Investigational Product (IP) handling, storage, and accountability. |
| Regulatory Affairs Officer | Submission of documents to HSA and ethics committee (EC). |

2.3 The Delegation of Authority Log must be maintained and signed by the PI. Any change in staff responsibilities must be documented and dated.

---

**3. ENROLLMENT PROCEDURES**

3.1 **Screening**
3.1.1 Potential participants are identified through approved recruitment materials or physician referral. All recruitment materials must be approved by the EC prior to use.
3.1.2 The Site Coordinator schedules a screening visit. The participant must be given the Informed Consent Form (ICF) and a copy of the Participant Information Sheet at least 24 hours prior to the screening visit, unless the protocol specifies a shorter period.
3.1.3 Screening procedures, including medical history, physical examination, and laboratory tests, must be performed only after written informed consent is obtained.

4.1 Monitoring visits are conducted by the Clinical Research Associate (CRA) or their delegate to verify that the trial is conducted in accordance with the protocol, Good Clinical Practice (GCP), applicable regulatory requirements, and this manual. The CRA serves as the primary point of contact between the site and the sponsor.

4.2 Types of monitoring visits:

| Visit Type | Purpose | Typical Frequency |
|------------|---------|-------------------|
| Site Initiation Visit (SIV) | Training on protocol, procedures, and IP handling prior to first participant enrollment. | Once, before enrollment begins |
| Routine Monitoring Visit | Ongoing review of participant records, IP accountability, and regulatory documents. | As per Monitoring Plan (e.g., every 4–6 weeks) |
| Close-out Visit | Final verification, return of IP, and confirmation that all outstanding items are resolved. | At trial completion |

4.3 The CRA shall notify the Site Coordinator at least 3 working days before a scheduled monitoring visit, unless the visit is triggered by an urgent safety or compliance concern. Urgent visits may occur without prior notice.

4.4 During a monitoring visit, the CRA will review, at minimum:

4.4.1 Source documents for enrolled participants, including signed informed consent forms, medical records, and laboratory reports.

4.4.2 eCRF entries against source data for accuracy and completeness.

4.4.3 IP accountability records, including dispensing logs, temperature logs, and returns.

4.4.4 Regulatory documents, including the Delegation of Authority Log, staff qualifications, and training records.

4.4.5 Adverse event (AE) and serious adverse event (SAE) documentation and reporting timelines.

4.5 Site staff shall make available all requested documents and provide a quiet workspace for the CRA. The Site Coordinator is responsible for coordinating access to source documents and ensuring that staff are available to answer questions.

4.6 The CRA will document findings in a Monitoring Visit Report. The report will note the date of the visit, the scope of review, findings, and any required corrective and preventive actions (CAPAs).

4.7 Monitoring Visit Report notes Clinical Research Associate monitoring_visit_status is completed. Record status: historical. The report is appended to this manual as Attachment A (latest version) and is considered part of the site's trial master file.

4.8 Follow-up actions identified during a monitoring visit must be completed within the timeframe specified in the report. The Site Coordinator shall track action items and confirm resolution in writing to the CRA. Unresolved findings may be escalated to the PI and, if necessary, to the sponsor.

4.9 The PI is responsible for ensuring that monitoring visits can be conducted as scheduled and that findings are addressed in a timely manner.

---

**5. DOCUMENTATION REQUIREMENTS FOR MONITORING VISIT REPORTS**

5.1 Each Monitoring Visit Report shall be signed and dated by the CRA. The report shall include:

5.1.1 Visit identification: visit number, date(s) of visit, and type of visit.

5.1.2 Participants reviewed: list of participant numbers and the extent of verification performed.

5.1.3 Findings: categorized as (a) no findings, (b) minor observations, or (c) major observations requiring CAPA.

5.1.4 Action items: description, responsible person, and due date.

5.1.5 Summary of IP accountability, including any discrepancies.

5.2 The report shall be distributed to the PI and Site Coordinator within 10 working days of the visit. A copy shall be filed in the regulatory binder.

5.3 The site shall retain all Monitoring Visit Reports for at least the duration required by applicable regulations and the sponsor's retention policy.

documents.title: Site Operations Manual
documents.content:
**6. VISIT SCHEDULING, CANCELLATION AND RESCHEDULING**

6.1 The Site Coordinator shall maintain a master visit schedule for the duration of the study. The schedule shall list, for each planned visit: the visit type (routine monitoring, site qualification, site initiation, close-out, or other), the expected date, the assigned Clinical Research Associate (CRA), and the current status.

6.2 A copy of the master visit schedule shall be provided to the CRA at the start of each monitoring visit and updated, if necessary, at the end of the visit. The schedule shall also be available for review by the PI upon request.

6.3 Scheduling of monitoring visits shall be coordinated between the Site Coordinator and the CRA. The Site Coordinator shall confirm the proposed visit dates with the PI and the pharmacy, as applicable, before confirming the visit with the CRA.

6.4 The site shall make every reasonable effort to accommodate the proposed visit dates. If a proposed date conflicts with a scheduled participant visit, a public holiday, or a planned site closure, the Site Coordinator shall inform the CRA within two working days of receiving the proposed schedule and propose alternative dates.

6.5 Cancellation Policy

6.5.1 Site Operations Manual specifies Lumina Clinical Research cancellation_policy is 48 hours notice. Record status: current. The 48-hour notice period is measured from the time the cancellation notification is sent by the Site Coordinator to the CRA and the CRO's monitoring department.

6.5.2 A cancellation is defined as the notification by the site that a scheduled monitoring visit will not occur on the agreed date. Cancellations shall be communicated in writing by email, with a read receipt requested, and shall include the visit number and the reason for cancellation.

6.5.3 If a visit is cancelled with less than 48 hours notice, the site shall document the reason and the circumstances in the visit schedule and, upon request, provide a written explanation to the CRO. Repeated late cancellations may result in a review of the site's scheduling practices.

6.5.4 Cancellations requested by the CRA or the CRO are not subject to this policy. In such cases, the CRA shall provide a revised schedule to the Site Coordinator as soon as practicable.

6.5.5 The cancellation policy is subject to change. The current version of this policy is in effect as of the date of this manual. Any proposed change shall be communicated in writing to the site at least 30 days before the effective date of the change.

6.6 Rescheduling Guidelines

6.6.1 When a visit is cancelled, the Site Coordinator shall work with the CRA to identify a mutually agreeable alternative date. The alternative date shall be recorded in the master visit schedule as a rescheduled visit, with the original visit number retained and the suffix "R" added (e.g., Visit 4R).

6.6.2 The rescheduled visit shall take place as soon as practicable, and in any case, not later than 30 calendar days after the original scheduled date, unless a longer delay is approved in writing by the CRO.

6.6.3 If the rescheduled date falls on a date when the site is closed, the Site Coordinator shall notify the CRA at the time of rescheduling.

6.6.4 The reason for the rescheduling shall be recorded in the visit schedule using the following codes:

6.6.4.1 "PI" – PI unavailable.

6.6.4.2 "SITE" – Site closure or staff unavailability.

6.6.4.3 "PT" – Participant visit conflict requiring site staff attention.

6.6.4.4 "CRA" – CRA unavailability (initiated by CRO).

6.6.4.5 "OTHER" – Any other reason, with a brief description.

6.6.5 A rescheduled visit shall not count as a separate visit for the purpose of the monitoring plan. The original visit number and the "R" suffix shall be used consistently in all correspondence and reports.

documents.content:
7.0 Data Entry and Source Document Handling

7.1 General Principles

7.1.1 All data entry shall be performed in accordance with the protocol, the Clinical Data Management Plan, and applicable regulatory requirements. The source document is the primary record of participant data, and the eCRF is a transcription of that source data.

7.1.2 Source data shall be entered into the eCRF in real time, or as soon as practicable after the data is generated. In no case shall data entry be delayed more than 5 business days from the date of the source document, unless prior written approval has been obtained from the CRO.

7.1.3 The Site Coordinator is responsible for ensuring that all data entry is complete, accurate, and consistent with the source documents. The Principal Investigator retains ultimate responsibility for the accuracy and integrity of the data.

7.1.4 Only authorised site staff who have completed the required training and have been delegated data entry responsibilities on the Delegation of Authority Log shall perform data entry. The Site Coordinator shall maintain a current list of authorised data entry personnel.

7.1.5 Data entry shall be performed in a quiet, private area of the site where the eCRF screen cannot be viewed by unauthorised persons. Participant confidentiality shall be maintained at all times.

7.2 Data Entry Procedures

7.2.1 Prior to initiating data entry for a participant, the data entry staff shall verify the following:

7.2.1.1 The participant has signed and dated the current approved Informed Consent Form.

7.2.1.2 The participant has been assigned a valid Participant Identification Number.

7.2.1.3 The visit has been completed and the source documents are available.

7.2.2 Data shall be entered into the eCRF exactly as recorded in the source documents. Abbreviations, units, and decimal places shall be transcribed without modification, unless a data entry convention has been documented and approved by the CRO.

7.2.3 All fields in the eCRF shall be completed. If a field is not applicable, the appropriate code (e.g., "NA" or "ND") shall be entered in accordance with the eCRF Completion Guidelines. Fields left blank may generate queries.

7.2.4 Measurements shall be entered in the units specified in the eCRF. Where the source document records a measurement in different units, the data entry staff shall convert the value and record the conversion in the source document, including the date and initials of the person performing the conversion.

7.2.5 If a value in the source document is illegible, the data entry staff shall not guess. The source document shall be returned to the individual who generated the data for clarification. The clarification shall be made in accordance with Section 7.4 (Corrections to Source Documents).

7.2.6 Data entry shall be performed on a per-visit basis. The eCRF for a visit shall be completed and signed before the next scheduled visit, unless the monitoring plan specifies otherwise.

7.2.7 The eCRF shall be signed and dated by the authorised data entry staff upon completion of data entry for each visit. The electronic signature shall include the date and time of the signature.

7.3 eCRF Access and Security

7.3.1 Access to the eCRF system shall be controlled by unique user IDs and passwords. Passwords shall be changed at least every 90 days and shall not be shared with or disclosed to any other person.

7.3.2 The Site Coordinator shall notify the CRO immediately, and in any case within 24 hours, if any authorised user leaves the site, is reassigned, or is suspected of unauthorised access.

7.3.3 The eCRF system shall only be accessed from site computers that have current antivirus software and operating system updates. Remote access to the eCRF is not permitted unless approved in writing by the CRO.

documents.content:
7.4 Corrections to Source Documents

7.4.1 Corrections to source documents shall be made using a single line drawn through the erroneous entry, leaving the original entry legible. The correct value shall be written adjacent to the original entry, followed by the date of the correction and the initials of the person making the correction.

7.4.2 Correction fluid, correction tape, erasers, or any other means of obliterating the original entry shall not be used on source documents.

7.4.3 If a correction is required after the source document has been scanned or otherwise archived, the correction shall be made on a new version of the document, and the previous version shall be retained in the site files with a cross-reference to the new version. The new version shall indicate the date and reason for the correction.

7.4.4 Where a source document is an electronic record, corrections shall be made using the audit trail function of the applicable system. The audit trail shall capture the original value, the corrected value, the date and time of the correction, and the user ID of the person making the correction. No electronic source data shall be overwritten without an audit trail entry.

7.4.5 The Investigator or designee shall be responsible for ensuring that corrections to source documents are made in a timely manner and that the corrected data is reflected in the eCRF at the next available data entry session.

7.4.6 Queries issued by the CRO or data management team regarding source data shall be resolved within 5 working days of receipt. If resolution requires clarification from the participant or an external provider, the Site Coordinator shall document the reason for the delay and provide an estimated resolution date.

7.5 Source Document Retention

7.5.1 Source documents shall be retained at the site for at least 15 years after the completion of the study, or longer if required by applicable regulations or the study contract.

7.5.2 Source documents shall be stored in a locked, fire-resistant filing cabinet or in a secure electronic repository with role-based access. The Site Director shall maintain an inventory of all source documents, including their physical or electronic location.

7.5.3 No source document shall be removed from the site without prior written approval from the Site Director, except when required for audit or regulatory inspection. In such cases, a receipt shall be issued and a copy retained at the site.

7.5.4 At the close of the study, the Site Coordinator shall prepare a complete set of source documents for archiving. The archive package shall include a cover sheet listing the contents and the date of archiving.

8.0 PHARMACY AND INVESTIGATIONAL PRODUCT MANAGEMENT

8.1 General Principles

8.1.1 The handling of investigational product (IP) shall comply with the protocol, the Investigator's Brochure, and applicable regulatory requirements. The Site Pharmacist or designee shall be responsible for the receipt, storage, dispensing, and return of IP.

8.1.2 IP shall only be administered to participants who have provided informed consent and who meet the eligibility criteria specified in the protocol.

8.1.3 Any deviation from the IP handling procedures described in this manual shall be documented and reported to the Sponsor in accordance with Section 8.7 (Deviations and Non-Compliance).

8.2 Receipt of Investigational Product

8.2.1 Upon receipt of an IP shipment, the Site Pharmacist or designee shall inspect the shipment for damage, verify the contents against the packing list, and confirm that the temperature monitoring device (if included) has not been activated beyond the allowable range.

8.2.2 The receipt shall be documented on the Investigational Product Receipt Log (Appendix C). The log shall include the date and time of receipt, the shipment number, the quantity received, the lot number(s), and the condition of the shipment.

We are submitting the above-referenced substantial amendment to the Health Sciences Authority for review and approval. This submission is made in accordance with the Singapore Guideline for Clinical Trials (SGCG) and the applicable provisions of the Health Products (Clinical Trials) Regulations.

The amendment introduces the following key changes to the protocol:

1. **Primary Endpoint Analysis Window:** The time window for the primary endpoint assessment has been revised from Week 12 to Week 16. This change is supported by emerging blinded data on the trajectory of the biomarker response and is intended to capture the maximal treatment effect.

2. **Criteria for Dose Interruption:** The criteria for dose interruption have been clarified to include a single occurrence of Grade 3 neutropenia lasting more than 5 days, or any Grade 4 neutropenia. Previously, the criteria required two separate occurrences of Grade 3 neutropenia.

3. **Concomitant Medication Restrictions:** The list of prohibited concomitant medications has been updated to include strong CYP3A4 inducers. This update aligns with the latest pharmacokinetic data from the ongoing Phase 1 study.

4. **Clarification on Participant Withdrawal:** Language has been added to clarify that participants who withdraw consent for the interventional portion of the study will be asked to consent to continued follow-up for safety and survival endpoints, where permitted by local regulations.

The rationale for each change is detailed in the accompanying Amendment Summary and the tracked-changes version of the protocol. The clean version of the protocol (Version 3.2) is also enclosed.

We respectfully request HSA approval of this amendment. Should you require any further information or clarification, please do not hesitate to contact the undersigned.

Yours faithfully,
